text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,819.25, up 1.85% on the day and 1.70% over the last five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.17% (5‑day +0.85%). Advances outpaced declines (268 vs 222) giving a “healthy” breadth score of 64.3, and the market stayed well above its 20‑day, 50‑day and 200‑day moving averages (≈61‑50‑50 %). Bank Nifty also jumped, ending at 63,703.25 (+1.79% daily, +2.30% weekly).  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added about ₹4,479 cr today, extending a 19‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) bought roughly ₹4,019 cr for a single‑day net inflow. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.91 for Nifty and 0.87 for Bank Nifty, indicating slightly more call interest. Max‑pain levels sit at 25,700 for Nifty and 63,500 for Bank Nifty, with resistance walls near 26,000 (call wall) and 66,000 for Bank Nifty. Leading sectors were banks, finance, FMCG and auto, whereas IT and oil‑gas lagged.  

Watch the 25,641.62 support (S1) and 25,996.63 pivot on Nifty; a break below S1 could test the 24,999 dma200. For Bank Nifty, the 63,256.17 support and 63,694.98 pivot are key, with 64,000‑66,000 range guiding the next session. Keep an eye on the USD‑INR at 92.81 and global cues such as Brent crude (≈ $90.6) and US equity futures, which may influence risk appetite. (PCR = put‑call ratio, max‑pain = price where option writers incur least loss.)
